items.title: The world’s two most powerful men just met. How did it go?
items.summary: The BBC’s China correspondent Laura Bicker unpacks how the trip panned out for Beijing and Washington.
items.content:
The world’s two most powerful men – Xi Jinping and Donald Trump – have just met in Washington after days of pomp and pageantry.

While there were many symbolic gestures, including Chinese pandas from President Xi, there were few big movements – although they committed to a two month extension of the tariff truce.

The BBC’s China correspondent Laura Bicker unpacks how the trip panned out for Beijing and Washington.

items.title: Media outlets banned by Trump denied access to White House dinner despite judge's order
items.summary: CNN and MS NOW reporters say they were barred from covering a state dinner after a judge ruled their passes should be restored.
items.content:
CNN and MS NOW reporters say they have been denied entry to cover a White House state dinner despite a judge ruling their access to the grounds must be restored.

A federal judge said in an overnight ruling that the White House ban on three outlets - CNN and MS NOW and Politico - was likely unconstitutional and that the administration must allow them access, for now. Trump barred them last week, accusing them of "fake news".

Journalists with the three outlets were allowed back in on Thursday morning.

Then in the evening, a CNN reporter and a producer and an MS NOW reporter said that they were denied entry to cover the guests arriving for a state dinner for Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

The outlets said they had properly submitted their reporters' names for credentials to cover the arrivals.

CNN said that about an hour before Xi was scheduled to arrive, the White House said it could cover the event only with a photojournalist and audio technician, but not a team that included a reporter and producer.

MS NOW White House reporter Laura Barron-Lopez said she was told by White House staff that she could not be let in, and to contact the White House communications director.

A White House communications account posted on X that "contrary to what the Fake News wants you to believe, they don't just get to have free rein into every part of the White House, every event, and every press call".

The incident was the latest in a series of events on Thursday surrounding the ban on some media outlets at the White House.

Despite the overnight ruling, CNN, Politico and MS NOW all reported being denied entry to the White House on Thursday morning, prompting a request for an emergency court hearing.

In response, the director of White House Operations said in a court filing that the press passes and confiscated badges had been restored by 09:45 local time (13:45 GMT).

Shortly afterwards, all three outlets said they were allowed back in.

However, networks including Fox News, NBC, CBS and ABC, which pulled out in solidarity, have yet to confirm they will resume broadcast coverage from the White House.

The chaotic standoff limited some TV coverage as Trump welcomed Xi to the White House ahead of a state dinner.

In his ruling, Judge Timothy Kelly said the ban on the outlets should be temporarily lifted because it "likely violated their constitutional due process rights".

He cast doubt on White House claims that the ban was justified in part on national security grounds, pointing out the president made no mention of this in his initial announcement.

"The record lacks factual support for defendants' contention that the revocation of plaintiffs' hard passes will in fact protect national security," Kelly wrote.

Judge Kelly ruled CNN, Politico and MS NOW were "likely to succeed" in showing the White House had not exercised "adequate due process" in the ban.

He ordered the immediate return of the outlets' press passes and a halt to enforcement of the ban for 14 days.

In a court filing on Tuesday, the US Department of Justice had accused the news outlets of threatening national security with their coverage.

Government lawyers cited stories about missile stockpiles, the construction of the White House ballroom and the recent Republican midterm convention.

What is the White House pool and why is it in a row with Trump?

Judge dismisses Trump lawsuit against Iowa newspaper and pollster over 2024 race

Trump first announced last Friday he was barring the three outlets from the White House, accusing them of writing "fiction or lies" about his administration.

By Saturday morning, each outlet reported that they were denied entry to t he White House grounds and that their press badges were confiscated.

All three outlets accused the Trump administration of violating their constitutional rights.

In a joint statement on Monday, they said they were pursuing legal action to "defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports".

More than 50 media organisations across the ideological spectrum filed an amicus brief in support of the lawsuit, including Fox News, the New York Times, the Washington Post and the Wall Street Journal.

There have been previous instances of administrations attempting to limit certain outlets' access.

The Obama administration tried to exclude Fox News from participating in a specific press pool interview with an administration official in 2009.

But after objections from the other four networks in the press pool, Fox News was allowed in.

items.title: IA da 120 miliardi di parametri anche senza cloud. Il segreto è MSI PRO MAX EDGE AI+
items.summary: Un sistema desktop compatto da 4 litri offre memoria unificata ad alta capacità, inferenza privata sul dispositivo e scalabilità multisistema per i flussi di lavoro professionali basati sull'intelligenza artificiale ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
L'intelligenza artificiale sta diventando parte integrante del lavoro quotidiano, ma non tutte le organizzazioni desiderano che ogni richiesta, documento o set di dati venga inviato al cloud. Per i team che lavorano con contratti riservati, banche dati proprietarie, risorse creative o analisi interne, l'IA locale può offrire un accesso più rapido, un maggiore controllo sul luogo in cui vengono elaborati i dati e una minore dipendenza dalla connessione a Internet o dai servizi cloud a consumo.

L'MSI PRO MAX EDGE AI+ è un desktop compatto con IA edge progettato per questo svolgimento. Costruito su una familiare architettura PC x86, il sistema combina fino a un processore AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, fino a 128GB di memoria unificata LPDDR5X e grafica Radeon 8060S integrata in un telaio in alluminio da 4 litri.

Molti PC compatti sono ottimizzati per carichi di lavoro standard per ufficio. Il PRO MAX EDGE AI+ è costruito attorno a un requisito diverso: fornire alle applicazioni di IA locali accesso a un calcolo e memoria consistenti senza dover utilizzare un PC di grandi dimensioni o una scheda grafica separata.

La configurazione di punta AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 include 16 core Zen 5 CPU, 40 unità di calcolo grafica RDNA™ 3.5 e una NPU XDNA 2 con una potenza fino a 50 TOPS. Su tutta la piattaforma, le prestazioni totali dell'IA raggiungono fino a 126 TOPS. Questa combinazione consente al software compatibile di utilizzare CPU, GPU o NPU a seconda del carico di lavoro, dalla produttività assistita dall'IA all'inferenza locale, al rendering e alla creazione di contenuti.

La capacità di memoria è spesso il fattore limitante quando un computer esegue un grande modello linguistico. Il PRO MAX EDGE AI+ supporta fino a 128GB di memoria unificata LPDDR5X-8000, con fino a 96GB configurabili come memoria grafica.

Invece di separare la memoria di sistema e la memoria grafica fissa in pool isolati, il design unificato permette alle applicazioni compatibili di utilizzare una risorsa condivisa più ampia.

MSI afferma che le configurazioni supportate possono eseguire grandi modelli linguistici con fino a 120 miliardi di parametri sul dispositivo. I test del prodotto MSI mostrano anche che GPT-OSS 120B ha utilizzato circa 65GB di memoria grafica. La dimensione del modello da sola non determina velocità o compatibilità: architettura del modello, quantizzazione, lunghezza del contesto, software, sistema operativo e configurazione della memoria influenzano tutti il risultato reale.

L'esecuzione locale di un carico di lavoro AI compatibile può conservare file e prompt selezionati all'interno dell'ambiente di un'organizzazione. Questo può essere utile per l'analisi privata di documenti, la generazione interna di recupero aumentata (RAG), la ricerca, la prototipazione e la produzione creativa.

L'esecuzione locale può anche ridurre la latenza di rete e mantenere disponibili gli strumenti quando la connettività cloud è limitata. Tuttavia, la privacy dipende ancora dalle applicazioni, dalle impostazioni e dalle politiche di gestione dei dati utilizzate; l'hardware da solo non garantisce un flusso di lavoro sicuro.

Un singolo desktop compatto può essere sufficiente per molte attività di IA locali, ma MSI supporta anche il clustering multi-unità per carichi di lavoro più grandi. La tabella di validazione pubblicata dall'azienda include configurazioni a due nodi per modelli selezionati 120B e 235B e una configurazione a quattro nodi per DeepSeek-V3.1 con 671 miliardi di parametri al Q4_0 quantizzazione.

Per i piccoli team e studi di IA, questo crea un percorso da un desktop a una configurazione di inferenza locale distribuita senza passare immediatamente a un'infrastruttura su scala rack.

L'inferenza AI, il rendering e le operazioni di big data possono imporre una domanda costante su un sistema.

MSI affronta questo problema con raffreddamento Frozr AI Pro, uno spreader di rame, tre heat pipe e un design a tripla ventola. I dissipatori di calore Glacier Armor aggiungono un supporto termico dedicato per i due slot SSD PCIe Gen 4 M.2, aiutando a mantenere le prestazioni di archiviazione durante l'accesso prolungato a file di modello e dataset locali.

Il telaio integra anche l'alimentatore da 300W, quindi non c'è un grande adattatore esterno che occupi spazio sotto la scrivania. Un interruttore fisico a tre stadi consente agli utenti di selezionare profili di alimentazione preimpostati e bilanciare prestazioni, temperatura e acustica senza dover prima navigare in un software utility.

Il PRO MAX EDGE AI+ supporta Wi-Fi 7 e fino a quattro display indipendenti tramite HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4a e due porte USB 40Gbps Type-C con modalità DisplayPort Alt. Fornisce inoltre più porte USB Type-A, connessioni audio anteriori e posteriori, Ethernet RJ45 e un lettore di schede SD 4.0 UHS-II. La combinazione è adatta ad analisi multi-display, montaggi e flussi di lavoro che spostano file di grandi dimensioni tra fotocamere, archiviazione e applicazioni AI locali.

L'MSI PRO MAX EDGE AI+ è un desktop edge AI da 4 litri per inferenza AI locale, creazione di contenuti, analisi dati e carichi di lavoro aziendali avanzati. È disponibile fino a un processore AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 e fino a 128GB di memoria unificata.

Sì. Modelli e applicazioni AI compatibili possono funzionare localmente sul PRO MAX EDGE AI+. MSI afferma che le configurazioni supportate possono eseguire modelli linguistici con fino a 120 miliardi di parametri sul dispositivo. Compatibilità e prestazioni variano in base al modello, alla quantizzazione, alla lunghezza del contesto, al software e alla configurazione del sistema.

Con un processore AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, la piattaforma offre fino a 126 TOPS di prestazioni totali di intelligenza artificiale. La sua NPU integrata XDNA 2 offre fino a 50 TOPS, oltre a CPU e risorse grafiche Radeon 8060S.

La memoria unificata permette alla CPU e alla GPU integrata di condividere un pool di memoria comune. Il PRO MAX EDGE AI+ supporta fino a 128GB di memoria LPDDR5X, con fino a 96GB assegnabili alla grafica, offrendo ai carichi di lavoro AI compatibili accesso a più memoria grafica rispetto a molti sistemi integrati convenzionali.

Sì. MSI supporta il clustering multi-sistema. La sua validazione pubblicata include modelli selezionati in configurazioni a due e quattro nodi, inclusi DeepSeek-V3.1 671B a quantizzazione Q4_0 su quattro nodi. I risultati dipendono dal modello, dal software e dalla configurazione del cluster.

Il sistema supporta fino a quattro display indipendenti tramite HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4a e due porte USB 40Gbps Type-C con modalità Alt-DisplayPort. Altre connessioni includono USB Type-A, RJ45 Ethernet, jack audio anteriore e posteriore, Wi-Fi 7 e un lettore SD 4.0 UHS-II.

È progettato per sviluppatori di IA, ricercatori, professionisti creativi, piccoli studi e organizzazioni che desiderano un sistema compatto per inferenza locale, flussi di lavoro privati di documenti, creazione di contenuti, analisi o produttività multi-display.

L'MSI PRO MAX EDGE AI+ sarà disponibile a partire dal mese di ottobre 2026. Configurazioni, disponibilità e prezzi possono variare. Per maggiori informazioni è possibile consultare la pagina prodotto e i canali social ufficiali MSI.

items.title: From Nagaland to a path to the Oscars: Indian film brings a rarely seen world to global cinema
items.summary: After a major win at Toronto, Angh, a film from northeastern India, is now on a path towards the Oscars.
items.content:
The film comes from Nagaland, a mountainous state of fewer than two million people on India's northeastern frontier, and is in Konyak, a tribal language unfamiliar to most Indians, never mind audiences abroad. It was director Theja Rio's first feature and most of its cast faced a camera for the first time.

And yet, at the Toronto International Film Festival this month, this quiet film won the Platform Prize, a major juried award.

The award is intended to recognise films with a particularly distinctive directorial voice. The jury praised Rio's "refreshing perspective" and the film's portrait of a world rarely encountered on the international screen.

The win also gives Angh an unusual route towards the 2027 Academy Awards. Under new rules, winners of designated prizes at six international festivals can qualify for consideration in the International Feature Film category without relying solely on their country's official submission.

This does not make Angh an Oscar nominee. But it does place a Konyak-language film from one of India's smallest states inside a global conversation from which such stories have been almost entirely absent.

Rio still sounds slightly startled by it. When we speak in Delhi, roughly 72 hours after the win, he has barely had a moment to breathe - Toronto, flights, interviews, more interviews.

"There were a lot of good films in the competition", he says, including films by far more seasoned directors. His producers were confident.

He is also less solemn than Angh might suggest. Before cinema, he wanted to be a rapper - "a kid from Compton instead of a kid from Nagaland", as he puts it. His tastes still range happily from Black Thought, the lead rapper of American hip-hop group The Roots, to his favourite filmmaker, the Iranian director Abbas Kiarostami.

Set in the early 1960s, Angh follows Anghba, the ageing hereditary chief of a Konyak village, and his young son, as the world around them changes. The Konyaks are one of Nagaland's 17 major tribes, concentrated in the eastern district of Mon, where such chiefs are known as Anghs. Even today, some older men bear facial tattoos associated with the Konyaks' historical practice of headhunting.

Anghba and his son are among the last in their region to hold to an ancestral faith as Christianity spreads.

Then an American missionary, played by Scottish actor Douglas Henshall, arrives. The father resists but the son is now curious.

Rio says the idea for the film came a few years ago, when he was visiting Mon for another project. What struck him was how closely different generations seemed to live alongside one another there.

Within a single family, he says, a grandfather might be a former headhunter, his face still tattooed; two generations later, his grandson might play guitar in a rock band.

"It feels like you've jumped on a time machine," Rio says. "The past and the present sort of coexist together."

The year also matters. Nagaland, which was earlier part of Assam state, formally became an Indian state in December 1963, during a period of profound political and social change.

By then, Christianity had been spreading among Naga communities for decades, bringing changes extending beyond religious belief into customs, rituals and everyday life.

Dr B Amo Konyak, a scholar of Konyak society, says the changes during this period were almost like a disappearance.

Some practices were lost; others "survived in fragments" - in the memories of elders, in family heirlooms. What had once been part of everyday life became heritage.

But Dr Konyak says culture did not simply stop. People carried parts of it into new religious and social worlds. Traditions survived, but changed meaning as they changed form.

"The past 50 or 60 years have brought extraordinary churn," he says, widening the distance between generations.

In Angh, he explores this through the relationship between the father and son who "intimately love and care about each other very deeply", even as their worlds begin to pull apart.

Critic Siddhant Adlakha was struck by the ambiguity the film captures. "Progress and tradition can be nonlinear, even entwined," he says, "rather than strictly opposing forces."

The film is yet to reach a wider audience, but its brief trailer offers a glimpse of how Rio constructed this world. Mist hangs over steep green hills; figures move through forests and village paths; fire and lamplight pick faces out of the darkness.

The landscape is beautiful but not merely picturesque - a small world held together by ritual, family and geography, while something larger presses in from beyond its edges.

Adlakha singles out the quiet close-ups of Anghlong Konyak, the first-time actor who plays the chief, and the "gentleness" with which Rio captures his "subdued rage".

What the camera saw mattered almost as much as where it was looking from.

Dr Konyak points to explorers, colonial officials, missionaries and photographers drawn to tattooed faces, ornaments, weapons and headhunting, while the lives behind them often receded from view.

Rio was conscious of inheriting that history. "There have been several films and documentaries made about Nagaland," he says, "but these sort of films tend to follow the gaze of the explorer rather than the subject."

With Angh, he wanted to reverse that gaze, asking viewers to "step inside the shoes of these characters".

The change is subtle but consequential. The Konyaks are no longer an exotic remnant of the past, but people living through what Dr Konyak describes as "love, grief, conflict, faith, uncertainty and generational change".

Konyak advisers worked on dialogue, costume and production design, and much of the cast was drawn from first-time Konyak performers. The forest, too, belongs to the people moving through it. Adlakha says Rio treats it "not just as a setting, but as a home with a history", much as an urban filmmaker might treat Mumbai or New York.

Rio and cinematographer Adam Pietkiewicz shot Angh on 16mm film, drawing on photographs and footage of missionaries and Naga communities from the 1950s and 60s.

They wanted to recreate the grain, texture and atmosphere of those archival images, while shifting the point of view from outsider to subject.

Unlike digital footage, the exposed film could not simply be reviewed on set. Every four or five days, the cans had to be sent to Mumbai for processing, while the crew carried on shooting without knowing exactly what they had captured.

During a night shoot with Henshall, an old Second World War Jeep was supposed to be driven into frame. It behaved perfectly through rehearsals. But when the cameras began rolling, the engine refused to start. After repeated attempts, the crew managed to capture just one take of the Jeep entering the frame.

Angh may be Rio's first feature, but its journey places it within a widening map of Indian cinema, especially in the northeast.

Adlakha points to filmmakers such as Assam's Rima Das and Meghalaya's Dominic Sangma whose work, he says, reveals "how complex and multifaceted the idea of Indian cinema happens to be".

Rio thinks Nagaland still remains at the edge of that scene. Its film industry is, as he puts it, "at a very nascent stage", with little of the reach enjoyed by India's established filmmaking centres.

But he hopes some of the attention around Angh travels back with it.

There are, he says, "so many talented filmmakers with so many beautiful stories that are yet to be told".

For now, though, Rio is looking forward to something more ordinary - getting back to Nagaland.

items.title: Cucce al posto delle culle, il fenomeno pet parenting
items.summary: Amare il proprio animale come un figlio, oltre 1 giovane su 2 li sostituisce alla prole, ecco perchè
items.content:
Questa deriva affettiva nasconde però un lato d’ombra evidenziato dalla ricerca internazionale di psicologia animale e antrozoologia. Secondo una recente review pubblicata sulla rivista scientifica internazionale Animals, condotta da un team di veterinari di atenei come la UNAM e l’Università di Pisa, l’eccessiva umanizzazione degli animali da compagnia porta frequentemente a disturbi comportamentali come ansia da separazione, aggressività e forme di stress cronico. Il motivo principale risiede nell’incapacità dei proprietari di interpretare i reali bisogni etologici e nutrizionali della specie, proiettando sull’animale bisogni, emozioni e aspettative umane. “ Il rischio del pet parenting non è amare troppo il proprio animale, ma amarlo nel modo sbagliato, proiettandogli addosso aspettative ed esigenze che appartengono ad un essere umano e non a un cane o a un gatto – spiega il dott. Vittorio Saettone, veterinario ed Head of R&D&QA di Schesir. “Rispettarli significa prima di tutto conoscerli: capire il loro linguaggio del corpo, i loro tempi e modi di socializzazione, le loro reali esigenze alimentari e comportamentali, che restano profondamente diverse da quelle di un bambino, per quanto affetto si possa provare. Condividere il pasto, offrire dolci o snacks pensati per il palato umano, o replicare un’alimentazione ‘di famiglia’ senza tenere conto delle specifiche esigenze nutrizionali di cane e gatto, può generare nel tempo carenze, sovrappeso o vere e proprie patologie causate da alimentazione non corretta. Una nutrizione realmente rispettosa della specie parte dalle materie prime, dagli ingredienti e dal loro specifico equilibrio nutrizionale, non dalle abitudini a tavola di chi li adotta. Lo stesso vale sul piano comportamentale: un cane o un gatto a cui non viene lasciata libertà di esprimere i propri istinti, annusare, esplorare, socializzare con i propri simili, può sviluppare ansia, frustrazione o comportamenti compulsivi, esattamente come accade quando si ignorano i suoi reali bisogni alimentari”.

Ecco 5 regole per rispettare davvero la natura del proprio animale, secondo gli esperti dello Schesir Respect My Nature Index:

1. Osservare il linguaggio del corpo prima di proiettare emozioni umane: interpretare ogni comportamento del cane o del gatto come se fosse “umano” (un broncio, un dispetto, una vendetta) porta spesso a non riconoscere i reali segnali di disagio, stress o dolore che l’animale sta comunicando a modo suo.

2. Rispettare i tempi e gli spazi di socializzazione della specie: cani e gatti hanno bisogno di relazionarsi anche con i propri simili, non solo con gli esseri umani; isolarli in una dimensione esclusivamente “familiare” può generare ansia da separazione o comportamenti compulsivi.

3. Nutrire in base alle reali esigenze biologiche, non alle abitudini umane: condividere il pasto, i dolci o gli snack da tavola con il proprio pet, per quanto sia un gesto affettivo, non tiene conto delle profonde differenze nutrizionali tra le specie e può comprometterne la salute nel lungo periodo.

4. Non sostituire il parere di un professionista con le proprie impressioni: davanti a un cambiamento nel comportamento o nell’appetito dell’animale, è sempre bene rivolgersi a un veterinario o a un educatore cinofilo/felino, invece di interpretarlo unicamente attraverso la propria sensibilità di “genitore”.

5. Rispettare i tempi di movimento e le posture naturali dell’animale: tenere il pet in braccio, in marsupio o in passeggino per lunghi periodi, oppure imporgli manifestazioni di affetto tipicamente umane come abbracci prolungati, ne limita la libertà di movimento e può essere percepito come invasivo o stressante, invece che come un gesto d’amore.

items.title: Guerra Ucraina - Russia, news di oggi. Zelensky: “Trump ha deciso di concederci licenza Patriot”
items.summary: Nuovi raid su Kiev: almeno 5 morti, tra cui un 14enne. Incontro a New York tra Dmitriev e gli inviati Usa Kushner e Witkoff
items.content:
Nuova notte di pesanti bombardamenti russi sull' Ucraina e su Kiev in particolare: muore un 14enne nella capitale, 6 feriti nell’attacco al palazzo della Corte Suprema. La guerra ibrida con il caso dell’aeroporto di Lipsia, le incursioni russe sempre più frequenti in Europa. Per questo il presidente francese Emmanuel Macron ha parlato di “guerra vera. Mosca è pronta a mobilitare altri 300mila uomini.

Media: 007 di Mosca dietro l’attacco incendiario a un’azienda della difesa di Monaco di Baviera

Russia, risultati finali delle elezioni: al partito di Putin 349 su 450 seggi

Cremlino: “Incontro trilaterale con Usa e Ucraina è possibile ma ancora non ci sono dettagli”

È salito a sette morti e 46 feriti il bilancio degli odierni attacchi russi a Kiev. Lo ha reso noto il sindaco della capitale ucraina, Vitali Klitschko, scrive l'Ukrainska Pravda.

Mosca: “Colpiti hub logistici, data center e navi usate per l'esercito ucraino”

Il ministero della Difesa di Mosca ha riferito che nei bomardamenti delle ultime ore le forze armate russe hanno a colpito hub logistici, data center e navi "impiegati nell'interesse dell'esercito ucraino" "Gli attacchi hanno danneggiato nella regione di Kiev, un centro logistico (Heavy Logistics Ukraine) nel villaggio di Trebukhov, i cui locali erano utilizzati da unità del ministero della Difesa e di altre agenzie di sicurezza ucraine per lo stoccaggio di merci a duplice uso e un data center di Datagroup, che elaborava e trasmetteva dati di intelligence per conto delle forze armate ucraine", si legge sul canale Telegram del ministero russo. Inoltre, secondo quanto riferito dal ministero della Difesa, "nella regione di Odessa è stata colpita una nave da carico che trasportava materiale militare al porto di Chornomorsk".

Filorussi: “Due morti e 5 feriti in raid ucraini su 2 mercati di Horlivka nel Donetsk”

Due persone sono rimaste uccise e cinque ferite a seguito di attacchi con droni delle forze armate ucraine su due mercati nella città di Horlivka, nella parte della regione di Donetsk controllata dai russi. Lo ha riferito il sindaco, Ivan Prikhodko, ripreso dall'agenzia Ria Novosti. I mercati colpiti, ha precisato il sindaco, sono quelli dei quartieri Nikitovsky e Centrale.

Un data center del provider internet ucraino Datagroup "è stato danneggiato" nei raid russi di oggi su Kiev. Lo rende noto lo stesso provider in un messaggio su Facebook ripreso dall'agenzia russa Tass. Datagroup ha aggiunto che sta lavorando per riprendere il servizio, attualmente spostato su siti di backup. Ieri altri nove provider ucraini avevano riferito di danni e interruzioni di servizio subiti a causa degli attacchi russi: Domonet, Pautina, Cityhost, Crazy Network, Etherlink, Faust, Kievnet, MiroHost e Utels.

La Russia sta monitorando con attenzione quali paesi intendano fornire, o abbiano già fornito, all'Ucraina licenze per la produzione di armi, oltre alle consegne di armamenti a Kiev. Lo ha dichiarato alla stampa il portavoce del Cremlino, Dmitri Peskov. Interpellato in merito alla dichiarazione del presidente ucraino Volodymyr Zelensky - secondo cui Donald Trump gli avrebbe promesso di concedere a Kiev una licenza per la produzione di missili destinati ai sistemi di difesa aerea Patriot - Peskov ha osservato che Trump non ha specificato "chi concederà la licenza". "Zelensky parla molto in questo periodo; pertanto, seguiamo naturalmente le informazioni su quali Paesi concedano determinate licenze e quali armi forniscano, e teniamo meticolosamente conto di tutto ciò", ha affermato Peskov.

Von der Leyen: “Con l'intesa sui 6,6 miliardi dell'Epf aumenta il sostegno a Kiev”

"L'accordo per lo stanziamento di 6,6 miliardi di euro dal Fondo europeo per la pace a favore dell'Ucraina è un'ottima notizia. Significa un maggiore sostegno alla difesa dell'Ucraina, dall'addestramento alle attrezzature. Viene a integrare quanto stiamo già facendo attraverso il nostro pacchetto di aiuti all'Ucraina, sia a favore dello Stato che della difesa. E da parte nostra ne arriveranno altri. Molto presto". Lo scrive su X la presidente della Commissione Ue Ursula von der Leyen.

Attacchi di droni russi hanno ucciso almeno cinque persone in pieno giorno a Kiev, tra cui un adolescente di 14 anni. Un attacco di droni contro un edificio per uffici, avvenuto in pieno giorno, ha causato almeno quattro morti e sette feriti, tra cui un bambino, secondo quanto riferito dal sindaco Vitali Klitschko. Questa mattina, mentre gli abitanti della capitale si recavano al lavoro, un altro drone ha colpito un edificio residenziale uccidendo un ragazzo di 14 anni, secondo l'amministrazione comunale. Oltre 30 persone sono rimaste ferite in questi attacchi, ha riferito il sindaco. Il presidente ucraino, Volodymyr Zelensky, ha riferito che è stato colpito un magazzino utilizzato da McDonald's vicino a Kiev. Ieri, attacchi russi con droni e missili avevano causato due vittime in città. Anche l'Ucraina ha intensificato negli ultimi mesi i suoi attacchi contro la Russia, prendendo di mira principalmente siti militari ed energetici. Nella notte tra ieri e oggi, l'esercito ucraino ha colpito due raffinerie russe, uno stabilimento militare e alcuni radar dell'esercito in diverse regioni della Russia, ha affermato Zelensky su Telegram. "Rispondiamo ai brutali attacchi della Russia contro i civili", ha dichiarato.

russians hit a civilian house in Kyiv again pic.twitter.com/0M1kdfzybL

Cremlino: “Licenza di missili Patriot a Kiev? Zelensky dice molte cose, monitoriamo”

Volodymyr Zelensky "recentemente sta dicendo molte cose". Così il portavoce del Cremlino, Dmitry Peskov, ha commentato l'annuncio del presidente ucraino secondo il quale Donald Trump gli ha comunicato che consentirà all'Ucraina di produrre missili per i sistemi di difesa Patriot. Peskov, citato dall'agenzia Tass , ha comunque sottolineato che la Russia "sta monitorando molto da vicino quali Paesi stanno fornendo quali licenze e fornendo quali armi" a Kiev, e tiene "tutto questo attentamente in conto".

Media: 007 di Mosca dietro l’attacco incendiario a un’azienda della difesa di Monaco di Baviera

Un attentato incendiario compiuto a Monaco di Baviera all'inizio di settembre potrebbe essere riconducibile ai servizi segreti russi. Lo scrive la Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung , citando fonti della sicurezza. Il 3 settembre, alcune persone a bordo di un'auto in movimento hanno lanciato ordigni incendiari contro un cantiere situato nelle immediate vicinanze delle sedi dei gruppi tecnologici e della difesa Rohde & Schwarz e Helsing, che fornisce droni alle forze armate ucraine. Un incendio è stato rapidamente spento e un secondo ordigno è stato disinnescato. Per l'attacco sono stati arrestati un uomo e una donna di nazionalità bulgara, ritenuti presunti collaboratori inesperti, i cosiddetti 'agenti di basso livello'. Secondo le autorità di sicurezza, dietro l'operazione ci sarebbe il servizio segreto militare russo Gru, che avrebbe utilizzato la stessa rete anche per pianificare azioni di sabotaggio in Slovacchia. Se il sospetto fosse confermato, si tratterebbe del secondo attacco in Germania in meno di un mese attribuito dalle autorità di sicurezza alla Russia, dopo il tentato attacco con un drone all'aeroporto di Lipsia del 4 agosto. Secondo fonti della sicurezza citate dalla Faz, il Gru sarebbe responsabile di diversi atti di sabotaggio in Germania, Polonia, Paesi baltici e altri Stati Ue, con l'obiettivo di colpire le infrastrutture utilizzate per il trasporto di forniture militari destinate all'Ucraina e scoraggiare il sostegno europeo a Kiev. A Lipsia, secondo le stesse fonti, il drone carico di esplosivo utilizzato nell'attacco era stato nascosto in precedenza in un deposito sotterraneo.

Secondo quanto riferito dalle autorità ucraine, almeno quattro persone sono rimaste uccise e altre 27 ferite negli attacchi russi di oggi a Kiev. Tra i feriti c'era un bambino di 9 anni. La Russia ha continuato i suoi incessanti attacchi con droni su Kiev: nella notte è stato colpito un edificio residenziale di 16 piani nel quartiere centrale di Pecherskyi, uccidendo un ragazzo di 14 anni e ferendo sette persone. Un attacco diurno con drone ha colpito un edificio per uffici nel distretto di Solomianskyi, uccidendo tre persone e ferendone altre sette nel parcheggio dell'edificio.

As of now, four people have already been reported killed as a result of a Russian drone strike on an office building in Kyiv. My condolences to their families and loved ones… Seven more people were injured, including a child. I thank all of our emergency services, which always… pic.twitter.com/RHSokGPe90

Tre persone sono rimaste uccise nei pressi di un edificio di uffici nel distretto Solomianskyi di Kiev, colpito da un drone. Lo ha reso noto il sindaco della capitale, Vitali Klitschko. La facciata dell'edificio è danneggiata e i vetri sono andati in frantumi, mentre diverse auto sono in fiamme nel parcheggio, ha riferito Klitschko. Secondo il sindaco, sette persone sono rimaste ferite.

⚡️ BREAKING: Russia attacked the Inkom business center in Kyiv 3 people were killed and 7 others were injured. The bodies of those killed are lying right in the street. pic.twitter.com/LUjyZ61gpl

items.title: È morta la giornalista di Sky Sport Elena Pero, nota soprattutto per le sue telecronache delle partite di tennis
items.content: È morta Elena Pero, giornalista italiana famosa soprattutto per le sue telecronache delle partite di tennis. Pero aveva 60 anni, due anni fa le era stato diagnosticato un tumore che aveva trattato con cure sperimentali e di cui aveva anche parlato pubblicamente. Aveva iniziato a lavorare a Telepiù , che poi diventò Sky Sport , nel 1991. Si occupava di telecronache da più di 20 anni, quasi sempre insieme al suo collega ed ex tennista Paolo Bertolucci: era tra le più note e apprezzate esperte di tennis in Italia.

items.title: Italy ministers agree to ban burqa and niqab in school and cap foreigners in class
items.summary: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni described the measures as "common-sense tools that do not divide but really help to integrate".
items.content:
The Italian government has approved a ban on the burqa and niqab in schools, along with a limit on the share of pupils who speak little Italian in any one class.

A 30% cap will be imposed on children without Italian citizenship or poor knowledge of the Italian language in the first year of primary, middle and high school.

Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni described the measures as "common-sense tools that do not divide but really help to integrate".

Opposition parties accuse the government of pandering to the policies of the hard-right Futuro Nazionale party, ahead of a general election next year.

Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara has said the limit is "purely linguistic" rather than one of citizenship, while he has sought to frame the ban on the niqab and burqa as a matter of gender equality.

"You must go to school with your face uncovered," Meloni said while announcing the plans on Sunday, adding that no-one could decide that a young woman should hide herself in the name of tradition.

There were several drafts of the decree ahead of Thursday's council of ministers meeting, however the core details were clear.

The veil ban would apply to the burqa and niqab, but not the hijab, which leaves the face visible.

The niqab is a veil for the face that leaves the area around the eyes clear. However, it may be worn with a separate eye veil. It is worn with an accompanying headscarf.

The burka is a one-piece veil that covers the face and body. Often there is a mesh screen around the eyes to see through.

Non-Italian citizens make up 11.6% of pupils in Italy's schools, according to the research institution Fondazione ISMU.

The 30% limit on pupils who speak limited Italian will cover separate stages of education differently.

In primary schools, it would cover non-Italian citizens who have either not been born in Italy or who have not attended at least two years of nursery school.

In lower- and upper- secondary schools, it would cover pupils without Italian citizenship who have not successfully completed at least three years in the Italian school system.

Local school offices would be asked to spread pupils with little Italian language skills more evenly among nearby schools. Where that is not possible, exemptions would apply, with extra Italian teaching.

The aim was to avoid "ghetto classes", the education minister explained.

The draft also goes further on parents, according to the Ansa news agency. Schools would have to report to social services cases in which persistent language barriers among those with parental responsibility hinder a child's integration. Free Italian courses would be offered.

The measure is a decree law, meaning it can take effect immediately, but must be ratified by parliament within 60 days.

Italy already has guidance on Italian language at schools. A 2010 ministerial notice under then-Education Minister Mariastella Gelmini set a 30% limit "as a rule" on pupils without Italian citizenship. The new decree puts the limit into law.

The political opposition says the plan is as much about politics as schools.

Opponents accuse Meloni of pandering to Roberto Vannacci, a retired military general who leads the hard-right Futuro Nazionale party and is seen as a threat to the governing coalition's right flank.

The leader of the centre-left Democratic Party (PD), Elly Schlein, called the plan propaganda and impossible to implement. PD deputy and chamber vice-president Anna Ascani also accused the government of propaganda at the expense of schoolchildren.

Valditara, speaking by video link from New York at a press conference rejected the charge.

"We are not chasing Vannacci; if anything, he is chasing us," he said.

Vannacci said he agreed with the measures, but they should have come years ago.

The League's Matteo Salvini, who launched a separate package of measures on what he called "political Islam" on Wednesday, accused Vannacci of "continually voting against the government".

Salvini said he hoped Futuro Nazionale would back the League's new proposals.

items.title: Priest killed and four injured in knife attack at Polish abbey
items.summary: A male suspect from Ukraine was arrested after the stabbings in the town of Jarosław, police say.
items.content:
A priest has been killed and four other people injured in a knife attack in south-east Poland, officials have said.

A 31-year-old Ukrainian man was arrested after the stabbings on the grounds of a Catholic abbey in the town of Jarosław.

Polish President Karol Nawrocki said Thursday's attack "has shaken us all and demands a firm response from the state", while his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky said "we are shocked by this evil".

Reports in Polish media said the attacker first injured a priest in a nearby cafe, and then another four people inside the abbey itself. A police investigation into the attacker's motives is now under way.

Polish police said four men and one woman were stabbed in the attack on Thursday morning on the abbey grounds.

The name of the murdered priest has not been publicly released.

Polish Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said psychological support was now being provided to all those affected by the incident.

Meanwhile, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the perpetrator "will be punished with the full severity of Polish law".

Echoing his words, President Zelensky said "the perpetrator of this evil must bear full responsibility according to the law", adding that Ukraine was counting on "a quick and thorough investigation of all circumstances".

In a statement, it said: "In such difficult moments, it is especially important to support each other, remain steadfast in respect for human life, and not allow pain to escalate into hatred or new violence. Responsibility for a crime must be based solely on the law."

Poland has recently seen a number of often violent incidents involving its citizens and Ukrainians, many of whom have fled their home country after Russia's full-scale invasion.

items.title: Four civilians killed in Pakistani strikes in Afghanistan, Taliban says
items.summary: Pakistan says it struck 10 targets, adding the strikes were "strictly limited to identified military objectives".
items.content:
Afghanistan's Taliban government said a wave of Pakistani air strikes had killed four civilians in the latest escalation between the two sides.

The strikes hit provinces including Kandahar, the Taliban's base of power, sources told the BBC. A resident told AFP news agency they heard a jet, followed by a large explosion and then a fire in the city.

Pakistan said its forces had struck 10 targets in Afghanistan, without specifying their locations, adding the strikes were "strictly limited to identified military objectives".

It's the second wave of Pakistani air strikes on Afghan territory in the past week, and comes after a deadly attack on a police facility in Pakistan on 18 September.

In a statement, the Taliban said there would be an "appropriate response" following the attack, while Pakistan said any further "provocative act" would be responded to.

Taliban government spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid said the attacks were in Afghanistan's Kandahar, Paktia and Khost provinces.

In Paktia, an official said jets had bombed the Afghan Armed Forces' 203 Mansouri Corps, which is controlled by the Taliban, without providing any information on casualties.

In Khost, a spokesman said houses were damaged in the strikes, with no casualties reported. Abdullah, a local eyewitness, told Reuters news agency the strikes happened around midnight.

"People were shouting, and there was panic all around," he said. "Afterwards, the village elder arrived and called out to the houses, asking if anyone was killed. Thankfully, no one was killed."

Another local, Salamat Khan, told Reuters that "there is no military base here, nor are there any military personnel", adding "there are only the homes of ordinary civilians".

Zabihullah Mujahid labelled the attack as "reckless, careless, and hostile", and said it "will have adverse consequences for the Pakistani military".

Pakistan's Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said the strikes were "deliberate, precise, calibrated, and proportionate, and strictly limited to identified military objectives directly linked to the attempted attacks against Pakistan".

The Taliban and Pakistan had enjoyed three months of relative calm, until fighting reignited following an attack on a mosque at a police compound in north-western Pakistan last week, which killed at least 31 people, according to AFP.

A group linked to Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) , which has waged a violent campaign against Pakistan for years, claimed the attack.

Islamabad has accused Kabul of harbouring the TTP. Afghanistan's Taliban government denies this, saying militancy is Pakistan's internal problem.

Following the attack on the police facility, Pakistan said earlier this week it launched air strikes in the Afghanistan-Pakistan border region, killing 28 militants.

Farid Dehqan, a spokesman for the Taliban government in Kunar province, told the BBC that three people were killed and four others were injured in the strike. The UN mission Unama also confirmed that at least three civilians were killed.

Then on Wednesday, Pakistan said it detected drones launched from Afghanistan into its territory and that all of them were "neutralised". Taliban officials denied that their government had launched drones against Pakistan that day.

Unama said in July that cross-border armed violence between Taliban government forces and Pakistani security forces killed at least 499 civilians and wounded 1,216 others between October 2025 and June 2026.

The worst single incident occurred in March, when more than 269 people were killed , external in a Pakistani air strike on Kabul, which the Afghan Taliban said hit a drug rehabilitation centre. Islamabad denied the charge, saying it "precisely targeted military installations and terrorist support infrastructure".

The neighbouring countries had agreed a ceasefire in March, but international mediation has failed to produce a lasting resolution.

During a meeting on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly earlier this week, Pakistan's Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar called for "concrete and verifiable" measures to ensure that Afghan territory is not used for "terrorism".

items.title: Watch: UN delegates walk out of Netanyahu speech
items.summary: The Israeli delegation cheered in support during Netanyahu's speech. Nada Tawfik in New York explains what happened.
items.content:
Dozens of United Nations delegates walked out of the hall Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was due to deliver a speech in.

Addressing the UN's General Assembly in New York, Netanyahu described those walking out as "moral cowards". Those who remained and felt similarly should leave, he said.

The Israeli delegation could be seen cheering Netanyahu in support.

Israel has faced condemnation for its actions in Gaza and Lebanon. A UN commission of inquiry has previously accused Israel of committing genocide against Palestinians in Gaza - Israel has strongly rejected the accusations.

The war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, in which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.

Israel responded by launching a military campaign in Gaza, during which more than 73,920 people have been killed, according to the territory's health ministry.

items.title: Why Australia chose the world's biggest political stage to reveal OpenAI hack
items.summary: Australia, which has strict social media restrictions and has proposed controls on algorithms and smart glasses, announced the breach at the UN.
items.content:
Australia made a dramatic revelation on Wednesday during the United Nations General Assembly.

Rogue AI agents had hacked one of its government bodies - the first known incident of its kind in the world. Private data, but not sensitive information, was taken from Medicare, Australia's universal healthcare scheme.

The breach happened in June, but OpenAI says it only became aware of it in August - and then took until 10 September to alert Australia's government, by sending an email to an address used by researchers and academics to alert authorities to concerns of vulnerabilities.

While worrying, the timing of the incident is somewhat of a gift for Australia.

A middle power that doesn't usually get as much of a platform as its influential allies, the country wants to be seen as punching above its weight on one of the most defining issues of our time - big tech regulation.

In the past year alone, it has implemented the world's strictest social media ban , announced what it says are the world's strongest algorithm controls , floated the possibility of "world-leading" limits on smart glasses , and is now the first government to confront AI firms over a rogue attack on its data.

It's entirely possible other governments have been the victim of rogue AI agents.

Former Australian government cybersecurity adviser Alastair MacGibbon told the BBC he'd heard whispers that several others have been notified of similar recent breaches by OpenAI agents.

"Some have chosen to not be public – that's every government's choice on how it wants to handle these things," he said. "The [Australian] government chose a time to release this to gain maximum publicity which is their wont to do."

Revealing a data breach can of course be a risky strategy for governments - it leaves them vulnerable to criticism that their security systems aren't up to scratch. But the fact that no sensitive information was leaked put Australia in a stronger position to use the incident.

"Nobody has died," says the University of Queensland's associate professor Michael Noetel, who studies AI risks. "This is another canary in the coal mine. This sort of loss-of-control incident, even though it's minor now, is what CEOs are worried about getting worse over time."

Though Australia has made a name for itself by taking a stand against social media companies, taking up the AI mantle now is another way for Australia to rein in big tech, says Tama Leaver, professor of internet studies at Curtin University in Perth.

"It's impossible to say for sure, but it seems incredibly likely that this was very carefully planned."

The fact that leaders were all together in New York this week has probably helped.

Albanese says he had a "frank" discussion with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman to express Australia's "extreme concern" about what happened. Altman acknowledged "issues with protocols" at OpenAI, he said.

The Australian leader also posed with Donald Trump for a selfie - and the two may have had face-to-face talks. But Australia risks the ire of the US president, who wants to encourage AI, "not rein it in", and even rename it "super intelligence" .

Earlier this week, Albanese had to deflect criticism from the Trump administration over his government's proposal to give users the ability to opt out of social media algorithms. The US said it amounted to "censorship of protected speech".

US criticises Australia's proposed algorithm opt-out laws as 'censorship'

Australia to double maximum penalty for platforms in breach of social media ban

Back home, Australia's very own eSafety commission is currently arming itself with lawyers, preparing to take on social media platforms objecting to its social media law for under 16s.

Australia isn't popular with big tech. But its bold policies on social media and internet safety have been largely supported among Australians themselves, especially parents.

The government is taking advantage of the hack to position itself as a leader on one of the biggest talking points of our time. And it's wasting no time in using the incident to advance the country's broader crusade.

Within hours of the announcement, Communications Minister Anika Wells told reporters: "This is an example of an unregulated industry where big tech clearly feels like they can do whatever they like, and that's not going to wash here in Australia."

items.summary: Proceeds from the tour, which begins in Dublin next month, will go to organisations supporting Palestinians, he says.
items.content:
Rapper Macklemore is launching a "Free Palestine" tour, days after being dropped from Ed Sheeran's Loop Tour following pro-Palestinian comments he made onstage earlier this month.

"So, as you all know, my schedule freed up a bit," he said upon announcing the tour on Thursday.

The American artist - whose real name is Benjamin Haggerty - said proceeds from the tour, which launches in Dublin next month, will go to organisations supporting Palestinians.

Macklemore's onstage comments and subsequent removal from the tour led Sheeran's support acts to drop out, while the British singer stressed that the decision to drop the rapper was made by his promoter, not by himself.

Everything we know about the Ed Sheeran and Macklemore controversy

In a statement on Thursday, the rapper said that the last couple of weeks had shown him there had been "a collective awakening around Palestinian liberation, the power of billionaires that try to censor that call, and what we expect from artists right now".

"What happened to me is bigger than one artist or one stage," he said. "When the billionaire class can decide which voices are allowed on stage and which ones are too dangerous to hear, everyone should be paying attention."

Macklemore said he had spent the last week contacting artists who had used their platforms to stand in solidarity with the Palestinian people, regardless of the consequences.

Due to how quickly the tour came together, several details were still being worked out, he added: "But this is a moment of momentum, and there is work to be done."

Macklemore's new tour will begin in Dublin on 26 October followed by Paris on 29 October and London on 30 October.

US dates will also be added, he said, with additional tickets going on sale next week.

While performing as the opening act for Sheeran at a concert in early September in New Jersey, Macklemore said: "A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so that I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very, very dear to my heart: Free Palestine."

The Thrift Shop rapper then performed a song dedicated to pro-Palestinian protesters at Columbia University.

After he was taken off the tour on 14 September, Macklemore accused stadium owners of rallying together to push him out. He was also accused by billionaire stadium owner Robert Kraft of hate speech and antisemitic rhetoric surrounding Israel and Gaza.

Sheeran early on said that the decision to drop Macklemore from his tour was made by concert promoter Messina Touring Group.

His early remarks led to all of his support acts to drop out of the tour in solidarity, and fans to express frustration. Ticket prices for the tour plummeted as well.

Sheeran addressed the controversy head-on during the start of his set in Philadelphia last week.

He said he had made "mistakes" handling the fallout, apologising to fans and taking a stand on the Israel-Gaza conflict, which he said was "a humanitarian issue".

He described the 7 October 2023 Hamas-led attacks as "horrific", and also called the situation in Gaza "unjustifiable and disproportionate".
